packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-05 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this fragment. The only identifying text seen is the modern pencil labels on the photographed pieces ("Stams, StA, Frg. 255-1r" / "255-2r" on face 1; "255-1v" / "255-2v" on face 2), which are visible in the images. This is a blind reading.

Method note (beyond the plain rules): to read the faded ink I made contrast-enhanced, channel-separated and enlarged crops of the supplied tiles with a local Python/PIL script (scratch files only). I opened nothing except PROMPT.md and the image files of this packet. Line numbers below are counted from the first text line I could see in each image (lines at a cropped top edge count); because the tiles overlap and the strip tops are stained, numbering is approximate (+/-1) and I give an approximate pixel y for anchoring.

==================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
==================================================================
- Two narrow vertical parchment strips per face, photographed side by side (image-001 = face 1 overview, image-010 = face 2 overview). Strips are c. 4-5 cm wide x c. 35 cm tall, cut obliquely at top and bottom (binding strips). Each strip preserves only a vertical slice of one text column; line beginnings or line ends are lost on one side.
- Script: small Gothic textualis bookhand, heavily abbreviated, brown ink, many short lines (c. 60+ lines visible per strip). Dense legal-type abbreviation: "ff." (repeated), "q." , "c.", "di.", numerals in dots (".ii.", ".xviii."), short reference strings with roman numerals. These look like citation chains embedded in prose (observation; interpretation as legal glossing is tentative).
- Paragraph openings: several lines begin with an enlarged or slightly projecting initial (e.g. image-002 a "Q" with large bowl; image-013 "E"/"Et" projecting into the margin; image-014 a large "E"/"C" opening "Exemplum?"/"Et ..."). No colour is visible in these photographs (no red visible on the strips).
- Short gaps/indents within lines mark section breaks (e.g. image-002 "Et post ..."; image-011 a blank line between blocks).
- Face 1 right strip (tiles 003, 005, 007, 009): text occupies only the right ~2/3 of the strip; the left part is blank margin with a dark vertical fold/crease line; lines are short (5-15 letters visible) - this is the inner edge of a column, line beginnings lost(?) or a narrow column. Face 2 right strip (012, 014, 016, 018) likewise shows text only on its right half.
- One underlined word on face 2 (image-015, approx. y 830, "sacramento(?)" underlined).
- No running titles visible (tops are cut and stained).
- Tentative interpretation: a single-column (or column-slice) prose text with dense citation abbreviations, possibly a legal commentary/summa. Not a main-text + gloss layout as far as these slices show.

==================================================================
2. SELECTED SPANS AND WHAT REMAINS UNREAD
==================================================================
Selected: face 1 left strip top (image-002), middle (image-004), lower (image-006, image-008 top); face 1 right strip short lines (image-003, image-007, image-009); face 2 left strip upper (image-011), middle (image-013), lower (image-015, image-017). 
Unread / only scanned: face 2 right strip (images 012, 014, 016, 018) beyond a few line beginnings; lower parts of image-008 and image-016/018; most of image-005 (very faded).
A wider, raking-light or UV view of the face 1 right strip and of the face 2 right strip would help; the ink there is very abraded.

==================================================================
3. TRANSCRIPTION
==================================================================
Conventions: (x) = proposed expansion; word(?) = uncertain; [illegible] = not readable by me; | = right edge of surviving strip where line is cut.
